summary: Evening connection flood causing API gateway 502s and runtime restart loop for Boxleaf (dedicated)
description:
Issue summary:
A Boxleaf tenant experienced a sharp spike in 502/5xx responses across multiple routes beginning ~2026-03-13T18:05:00Z. API Gateway returned 502s and 504s, and upstream serving-runtime pods entered restart loops. Error window lasted ~45 minutes with highest error rate at ~18:20 UTC. Customer reported production impact: failed interactive requests and degraded throughput.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency/failures for Boxleaf production workload (dedicated capacity).
- Traffic loss estimated ~30% of requests for impacted tenant during the window.
- Boxleaf reported user-visible errors for their chat endpoints.

Environment:
- Deployment: dedicated cluster for Boxleaf (tenant id: boxleaf-prod).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Models: redwood/llama-13b-v2 pinned to v2026-02-28.
- Ingress: api-gateway cluster behind edge-proxy pool.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) High rate of concurrent short-lived connections from tenant between 18:04-18:22 UTC.
2) API Gateway hit connection queue and began returning 502 to new requests when upstream TLS handshakes timed out.
3) Serving-runtime processes showed repeated segfault-like exits followed by immediate restarts; OOMs not present.
4) Autoscaler attempted to spin up replacement pods, which joined but hit the same failure pattern.

Logs/metrics (selected):
- api-gateway/edge-proxy: connection_queue_length spiked to 12k; TLS handshake error rate increased (ERR_TLS_HANDSHAKE=3.2k/min).
- serving-runtime: process exit codes 139 (segfault) recorded on 6 distinct pods between 18:08-18:18 UTC.
- node exporter: no host OOMs or CPU saturation above 70%.
- kernel oops/oom logs: none.
- trace: request IDs see https://observability.redwood.ai/traces/INC-20260313-07 (internal link).

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Connection flood from a customer-side traffic pattern (short connections) overwhelmed the API gateway connection backlog leading to TLS handshake failures and wave of upstream disconnects. Evidence: edge-proxy socket backlog metrics correlate with 502 spike.
- Hypothesis B: A latent memory corruption bug in serving-runtime exposed under a particular request pattern, causing process crashes (exit 139). Evidence: core dumps present but limited; crash addresses point into the custom kernel-attention module linked in serving-runtime.
- Hypothesis C: Race in warmup/kvcache initialization during rapid new-connection storms causing invalid memory reads. Evidence: startup logs show repeated kvcache init warnings immediately prior to exits.

Actions taken so far: 
- Support (Ava) opened incident, paged on-call runtime (Devon).
- Scaled down Boxleaf traffic to 20% via rate-limit hold at the edge to reduce error amplification at 18:25 UTC (mitigation reduced error rate by ~70%).
- Collected core dumps and uploaded to internal artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/incidents/INC-20260313-07/cores/.
- Disabled the most-recent runtime kernel optimization flag (kernel-opt=attn_v2) for new pods as an isolation step; new pods stayed healthy in short tests.
- Warmed an alternate dedicated pool with kernel-opt=attn_v1 and tested with synthetic short-connection burst; no crash observed in 30m test.

Open questions / next steps: 
- Confirm root cause: memory corruption in attn_v2 kernel vs. edge connection backlog amplification.
- Run extended fuzzing of attention kernel in staging with short-connection workload.
- Roll forward a temporary fix: keep Boxleaf pinned to kernel-opt=attn_v1 while we complete PR and CI validation for mount/attn fixes.
- Post-incident: full postmortem + recommendation to add connection queue-based auto-throttle at gateway per-tenant.

Suggested owner and ETA:
- Runtime engineering (Devon) owner for root cause validation (ETA 72h).
- Support/CS (Ava) owner for customer communication and temporary routing policy (ETA 24h).

Customer communication:
- Notified customer at 2026-03-13T18:40Z with mitigation steps and ETA for full rollback to stable kernel. Boxleaf requested follow-up and impact quantification.
